newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico spends $150 million to combat poverty.
newsitem.headline: Mexico spends $150 million to combat poverty.

text.p: Mexico launched a multimillion-dollar fund on Wednesday aimed at helping at least 20 million of its 90 million people who live in extreme poverty.
President Ernesto Zedillo met peasants in an impoverished region of central Hidalgo state to present an annual 1.2 billion peso (about $150 million) programme in loans for education, health and food.
"Poverty is our most serious lag, our greatest challenge and its battle should be our greatest commitment," Zedillo said.
The programme is not a new one, but a repetition of the millions of pesos spent to help communities in 1982 and 1988.
"Today we initiate a programme to break with the vicious circle of ignorance, sickness and malnutrition that has trapped many million of Mexicans," Zedillo said.
He said the programme aims at helping 170,000 families in its first stage, and 230,000 more families by year's end.
Mexico City Mayor-elect Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, an outspoken leader of the growing left wing, said from Argentina that Zedillo's Cabinet has been insensitive to misery and unemployment.

"The governments and states should take responsibility for social problems and not be insensitive, as the Mexican government has been in the face of misery and unemployment," Cardenas told reporters during a visit to Buenos Aires.

Mexico is emerging from its worst financial crisis since the Great Depression after the peso was devalued in December 1994, causing a recession that threw more than a million Mexicans out of work and closed 20,000 businesses.
